title: Open Logic Lindstrom characterization of first-order logic by compactness and the downward Lowenheim-Skolem property

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite relational quantifier-rank types and back-and-forth

core_obligations: Retain the author finite-rank definability lemma and its finite conjunction/disjunction argument
Retain complete finite-sequence/partial-isomorphism coding and downward-LS contradiction with its author diagram
Retain the full coded family of rank-n counterexamples and the compactness-produced nonstandard rank construction
Apply the included supporting partial-isomorphism theorem under the actual chapter framework, without adding proof cases or silently changing the original hypotheses

difficulty_reason: H2: the own proof encodes finite sequences and partial isomorphisms inside expanded structures so that a downward LS argument transfers the problem to countable isomorphic models. The main construction then packages all finite-rank counterexamples into one coded structure, uses compactness to obtain a nonstandard rank, and turns the resulting family of finite back-and-forth approximations into a partial isomorphism contradicting the distinguishing abstract sentence. The finite-rank definability and LS coding theorems are supplied as full core, counted under one parent rather than separate lemma IDs. This is a nonroutine abstract-model-theory construction beyond ordinary first-order compactness or syntax induction.

editorial_notes: All mathematical statement and proof text is reproduced verbatim from the Open Logic Project, unit model-theory, file lindstrom-proof.tex, fixed at commit 1e960beff9ed7835bf3e3f1335e21af3439cd107. Only the packaging (the adapter preamble and the standalone wrapper) is this module's.
Numbering inside this standalone excerpt is editorial, not the Open Logic Project print numbering.

The adapter preamble loads the project's OWN style layer verbatim (sty/open-logic-formulas.sty, sty/open-logic-tokenize.sty, sty/open-logic-selective.sty and open-logic-config.sty, including its tag truth assignment), so the author's !! text-token shorthand, !A math metavariables, rule names (Intro, Elim, FalseInt) and the tag conditionals resolve exactly as in the book. Three substitutions are forced by the pinned toolchain and are recorded: isomath.sty is absent so \mathsfit is \mathsf; xpunctuate.sty is absent and unused so its RequirePackage is dropped; thmtools/ntheorem are absent so the environments are amsthm with the project's family numbering. The proof trees are the project's own bussproofs-extra.

The H2 judgement and its reason were made in this module by reading the author's own statement and complete proof at the pinned line span. Original candidate key: model-theory/lindstrom|lindstrom-proof.tex|thm:lindstrom.

Reference labels in the proof resolve to navigation pointers to the original author source; these pointers do not reproduce proofs of the prerequisites. The author's own ollabel is kept unprefixed (not part:chapter:section) so those pointers resolve; the label text itself is the author's own argument.
